raw_output: {"kind":"answer","urgent":false,"ask":null,"answer":{"cause":"A knocking from the front together with a warning light most likely points to an engine problem, such as low oil pressure or overheating, and the car should not be driven further.","confidence":"possible","alternatives":["A loose wheel or a worn suspension or steering part at the front","A failing CV joint or wheel bearing"],"steps":["First, put the hazard lights on and get everyone out on the side away from traffic. Stand well off the road, not between the car and traffic.","Switch the engine off and leave it off. Don't try to drive on with the knocking.","Place the warning triangle behind the car. In a built-up area it goes right behind the car; outside one it goes 30 to 50 m back.","Look at the warning light's colour and symbol. A red light, especially an oil can or thermometer, means do not restart the engine. An amber light is less urgent, but with knocking it's still not safe to drive.","Call roadside assistance for a tow or a mechanic to come to you. You can also check car repair under Nearby below.","If you get a tow and the car is an automatic, tell the tow company. A flatbed is preferred."],"escalate_if":["Smoke, steam or a burning smell from the engine area","Fuel or other fluid leaking under the car","Anyone is hurt or feels unwell","The car is partly standing in a lane with traffic (call 112)"],"photo_observation":null,"extra_categories":["repair"]}}
